title: Sidorenko's Conjecture (Conjecture 1.2)
statement_text: For every bipartite graph $A$ and graph $H$, we have $t(A, H) \geq t(K_2, H)^{e(A)}$.
context_text: Independently posed by Erdős–Simonovits and Sidorenko, this conjecture states that every bipartite graph has asymptotically at least as many copies in any dense graph as expected in an Erdős–Rényi random graph of the same edge density. The Möbius ladder on 10 vertices remains a notorious small open case.
paper_contribution: Shows that an oriented graph $B$ admitting a homomorphism $B \to \vec{K}_2$ has the directed Sidorenko property if and only if its underlying undirected bipartite graph has the asymmetric Sidorenko property (Theorem 1.5), reducing the directed problem to the asymmetric undirected setting.

paper_title: A note on directed analogues of the Sidorenko and forcing conjectures

title: Forcing Conjecture (Skokan–Thoma)
statement_text: A graph $A$ is forcing if and only if it is bipartite and contains a cycle.
context_text: Initially posed by Skokan and Thoma, the forcing conjecture characterises which graphs $A$ have the property that edge density together with $A$-density being asymptotically extremal forces the host graph sequence to be quasirandom. That bipartiteness and containing a cycle are necessary is straightforward.
paper_contribution: Proves two necessary conditions for the directed forcing property (Theorem 1.6) and shows that an oriented graph $B$ with a homomorphism $B \to \vec{K}_2$ has the directed forcing property if and only if its underlying undirected bipartite graph has the asymmetric forcing property (Theorem 1.8).

title: Conjecture 1.4
statement_text: If $B$ is a bipartite oriented graph with a homomorphism $B \to \vec{K}_2$, then $B$ has the directed Sidorenko property.
context_text: An oriented graph is a simple graph with each edge oriented; $\vec K_2$ is the single arc (directed edge). For oriented graphs $B,G$, a homomorphism $B\to G$ is a vertex map sending every arc $(x,y)$ of $B$ to an arc $(f(x),f(y))$ of $G$, and the homomorphism density $t(B,G)$ is the fraction of all maps $V(B)\to V(G)$ that are homomorphisms (similarly $t(A,H)$ for undirected graphs). An oriented graph $B$ has the directed Sidorenko property if $t(B,G)\ge t(\vec K_2,G)^{e(B)}$ for every oriented graph $G$, i.e. $G$ contains at least as many copies of $B$ as expected in a random oriented graph of the same edge density. This is a directed analogue of Sidorenko's conjecture, which asserts $t(A,H)\ge t(K_2,H)^{e(A)}$ for every bipartite graph $A$ and every graph $H$. Having a homomorphism to $\vec K_2$ (i.e. every vertex of $B$ is a source or a sink) is necessary, since otherwise $B$ has no copy in the complete bipartite graph with all arcs oriented from one side to the other. For a bipartite undirected graph $A=(A_1\sqcup A_2,E)$ with a fixed ordered bipartition and a bipartite graph $H=(U_1\sqcup U_2,F)$, $t_{\mathrm{bip}}(A,H)$ is the fraction of maps $f$ with $f(A_i)\subseteq U_i$ ($i=1,2$) that are homomorphisms; $A$ has the asymmetric Sidorenko property if $t_{\mathrm{bip}}(A,H)\ge t_{\mathrm{bip}}(K_2,H)^{e(A)}$ for every bipartite $H$, i.e. the count of copies of $A$ respecting sides is at least that expected in a random bipartite graph of the same bipartite density $|F|/(|U_1||U_2|)$. Such a homomorphism gives the underlying graph $\overline B$ of $B$ a bipartition (preimages of the tail and of the head of $\vec K_2$), and the authors prove that $B$ has the directed Sidorenko property if and only if $\overline B$ has the asymmetric Sidorenko property; thus the conjecture is equivalent to the asymmetric Sidorenko conjecture.
paper_title: A note on directed analogues of the Sidorenko and forcing conjectures

title: Conjecture 1.7
statement_text: If $B$ is an oriented graph with a homomorphism to an edge and whose underlying undirected graph has a cycle, then $B$ has the directed forcing property.
context_text: An oriented graph is a simple graph with each edge oriented; $\vec K_2$ is the single arc (directed edge). For oriented graphs $B,G$, a homomorphism $B\to G$ is a vertex map sending every arc $(x,y)$ of $B$ to an arc $(f(x),f(y))$ of $G$, and the homomorphism density $t(B,G)$ is the fraction of all maps $V(B)\to V(G)$ that are homomorphisms (similarly $t(A,H)$ for undirected graphs). A sequence of oriented graphs $(G_n)$ is quasirandom with density $p$ if its directed graphons (the step functions $W_{G_n}:[0,1]^2\to\{0,1\}$ obtained by splitting $[0,1]$ into $v(G_n)$ equal intervals and setting $W_{G_n}(x,y)=1$ on $I_i\times I_j$ iff $(i,j)$ is an arc) converge in cut norm to a constant. An oriented graph $B$ has the directed forcing property if, for every $p\in[0,1]$, every sequence of oriented graphs $(G_n)$ with $t(\vec K_2,G_n)\to p/2$ and $t(B,G_n)\to(p/2)^{e(B)}$ (the values for a random orientation of a random graph of edge density $p$) is $p$-quasirandom. This is a directed analogue of the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma, which states that an undirected graph is forcing (counts of it at the random value force quasirandomness) if and only if it is bipartite and contains a cycle. The authors prove that having a homomorphism to $\vec K_2$ (every vertex of $B$ is a source or a sink) and having a cycle in the underlying undirected graph $\overline B$ are both necessary for the directed forcing property, and that, for $B$ with a homomorphism to $\vec K_2$, $B$ has the directed forcing property if and only if $\overline B$ (with the bipartition given by the homomorphism) has the asymmetric forcing property, the analogous property for bipartite graphs with ordered sides counted side-respectingly.
paper_title: A note on directed analogues of the Sidorenko and forcing conjectures

title: Equivalence of asymmetric and classical Sidorenko properties
statement_text: It is conjectured that the asymmetric Sidorenko property and the classical Sidorenko property are equivalent for bipartite graphs.
context_text: For graphs $A,H$, the homomorphism density $t(A,H)$ is the fraction of all maps $V(A)\to V(H)$ that send edges to edges; a bipartite graph $A$ has the (classical) Sidorenko property if $t(A,H)\ge t(K_2,H)^{e(A)}$ for every graph $H$, and Sidorenko's conjecture asserts that every bipartite graph has it. For a bipartite undirected graph $A=(A_1\sqcup A_2,E)$ with a fixed ordered bipartition and a bipartite graph $H=(U_1\sqcup U_2,F)$, $t_{\mathrm{bip}}(A,H)$ is the fraction of maps $f$ with $f(A_i)\subseteq U_i$ ($i=1,2$) that are homomorphisms; $A$ has the asymmetric Sidorenko property if $t_{\mathrm{bip}}(A,H)\ge t_{\mathrm{bip}}(K_2,H)^{e(A)}$ for every bipartite $H$, i.e. the count of copies of $A$ respecting sides is at least that expected in a random bipartite graph of the same bipartite density $|F|/(|U_1||U_2|)$. The asymmetric Sidorenko property implies the classical one (apply it to the bipartite double cover of $H$, with two copies of $V(H)$ and an edge between copies of $u$ and $v$ whenever $uv\in E(H)$), so it is a priori stronger. There is no known black-box reduction in the other direction, but essentially all bipartite graphs known to have the Sidorenko property are also known to have the asymmetric one (e.g. Conlon, Fox and Sudakov observed it for bipartite graphs with a vertex complete to the other side). The question matters for the paper because the authors show that the directed Sidorenko property of an oriented graph with a homomorphism to an arc is equivalent to the asymmetric Sidorenko property of its underlying bipartite graph.
notes: Reported as a widely held community belief without explicit attribution to specific authors; no formal labelled environment.
